form_analysis.feedback: Good specific aftercare for a common AHA peel. Clearly addresses the potential for stinging and subtle flaking. Reinforces the importance of neutralising any residual acid and managing the temporary increase in sun sensitivity. Practical and straightforward.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare advice is for a glycolic acid (AHA) peel. Glycolic acid exfoliates the surface layers, improving texture and brightness. Your skin will be temporarily more sensitive.

instructions.general_directive: Please follow the General Chemical Peel Principles. The notes below are specific to glycolic acid peels.

sections.title: Immediate Post-Treatment Symptoms and Timeline
sections.content: You will feel a tingling or mild stinging during and immediately after the peel, which should subside within minutes to an hour. Skin will be pink and may feel tight for 12-48 hours. Light flaking or 'sheet peeling' may occur 2-4 days post-treatment, depending on the strength used.

sections.title: Specific Instructions
items: Neutralising: The peel was neutralised, but if you feel persistent burning at home, you may rinse with cool water or apply a cool compress.
Moisturize: Glycolic acid can be drying. Use a good moisturizer to combat tightness and support barrier repair.
Sun Sensitivity: AHAs increase photosensitivity for up to 1 week post-peel. Sun protection is non-negotiable. Use SPF 30+ daily.
Product Restart: Avoid using any other glycolic acid or AHA products at home for 5-7 days post-peel to avoid over-exfoliation.

sections.title: Activity Restrictions
sections.content: Avoid strenuous exercise, sweating, and heat exposure (saunas, steam) for 48 hours to minimise stinging and irritation.

sections.title: Makeup
sections.content: It is advisable to avoid makeup for 24 hours. If necessary, use a gentle, non-comedogenic formula.

sections.title: General Side Effects and Results Assessment
items: A mild breakout (purging) 3-7 days post-peel is possible as congestion is brought to the surface.
If you experience severe redness, swelling, blistering, or crusting, contact your practitioner.
Results include smoother texture, diminished fine lines, and a brighter complexion. A series of 4-6 peels (every 2-4 weeks) is typical for significant improvement.
Glycolic acid is excellent for sun damage and rough texture.
